points.t: Crops of **very itchy firm papules** in clusters or lines, on a child’s legs or on sleep-exposed skin; often **only one household member** reacts.
**Hypersensitivity to arthropod saliva** (immediate + delayed); new bites flare old ones; children usually desensitise.
**Eradicate the source** (vet flea products, vacuum; professional bed-bug control) + short topical steroid and antihistamine.
**Anaphylaxis**, spreading cellulitis, fever after bites abroad; don’t give antibiotics for ordinary redness lasting ~10 days.

cause.lead: An allergy to bites, not an infection.
points: Sensitised people react; others in the house may be bitten but unmarked.
**Fleas**: pets, or dormant pupae woken in a new house; spring–autumn.
**Bed bugs**: all year, night feeds, travel and second-hand furniture.
Outdoor: mosquitoes and midges on exposed sites.

features.lead: Grouped, intensely itchy, often in threes.
points: Firm red papules **3–10 mm**, ± punctum, vesicle or blister; excoriations and later pigmentation.
**Fleas**: ankles, lower legs, waistband. **Bed bugs**: face, neck, arms; blood / faecal spots on sheets.

visuals.caption: Flea bites cluster around the ankles and lower legs, because fleas jump to about that height; papules are often grouped in threes.
visuals.alt: Ankle with grouped red papules and scratch marks

points: Pets, new house, travel, season, who else itches.

cards.name: Scabies
cards.clue: Web spaces, wrists, genitals, burrows; **whole household itchy**.

cards.name: Acute urticaria
cards.clue: Wheals fade within 24 h; no crusted papules.

cards.name: Chickenpox
cards.clue: Fever; crops at different stages including scalp.

cards.name: Delusional infestation
cards.clue: Conviction of infestation, no insects confirmed.

points: **Fleas**: vet flea products for **all** pets; hot-wash bedding; vacuum; household IGR spray for weeks.
**Bed bugs**: council or professional (BPCA / NPTA) pest control.
Non-sedating antihistamine by day; short sedating antihistamine at night (check age licence).
Short **mild–moderate topical steroid** on new itchy spots (potent only briefly on thick adult lesions).
Spreading cellulitis / impetigo: **flucloxacillin** first-line (NICE NG182); Pharmacy First infected insect bite pathway (England, ≥ 1 year) within PGD.

limits.t: Redness and itch can last ~10 days without infection.

items.t: Systemically unwell, spreading cellulitis, bites in mouth / throat or around eyes.
Fever or a persisting unusual lesion after bites abroad.
Atypical persistent eruption or suspected delusional infestation: GP / dermatology.

pearls.t: **The pet may look fine; the house is the reservoir.**
Ankles and pets → fleas; sleep-exposed sites and sheet spots → bed bugs.
Explain why only one person reacts: sensitisation, not ‘dirty house’.

quiz.q: Why does only one family member get spots?
quiz.a: Only sensitised people react to the bites.

quiz.q: Best treatment for flea bites that keep recurring?
quiz.a: Treat all pets with vet products + vacuum + household spray.
Only for genuine secondary infection (flucloxacillin, NG182).
